ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Orthopedic trauma foundations: 4

A suspected fracture is visible on one projection, but its displacement cannot be confidently characterized. Which basic imaging principle helps avoid an incomplete three-dimensional assessment before deciding on the appropriate treatment strategy?

  1. Include adjacent joints when indicated
  2. Describe distal-fragment position relative to the proximal fragment
  3. Assess extension into the joint surface
  4. Inspect soft tissues as well as bone
  5. Obtain adequate orthogonal views
Answer and explanation

Obtain adequate orthogonal views

A fracture or displacement can be missed or mischaracterized on a single projection.

Option explanations

Obtain adequate orthogonal views: A fracture or displacement can be missed or mischaracterized on a single projection.

Include adjacent joints when indicated: Shaft injuries may be accompanied by proximal or distal joint disruption. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Describe distal-fragment position relative to the proximal fragment: Standard descriptions use the distal fragment relative to the proximal fragment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Assess extension into the joint surface: Articular involvement affects congruity, prognosis and treatment planning. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Inspect soft tissues as well as bone: Gas, swelling, effusion and foreign bodies can provide important injury clues. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
